description: Signed receipts for every stage of a data pipeline, verified as a green, yellow, or red light. Python and JavaScript, interchangeable chains. Proves continuity, not correctness.
rules: Follow AGENTS.md in order to integrate: install, tamper-signal init, tamper-signal ingest the source export, wrap each transform with @receipt_step (Python) or receiptStep (Node), mount the light with the room behind it, publish table.json, then tamper-signal verify.
The command is tamper-signal on both stacks; receipts is a deprecated Python alias.
verify exits 0 green, 1 red, 2 yellow; use --json for a structured verdict instead of parsing text.
Never commit a private key: keys/ and *.key belong in .gitignore. In CI, pass the key through the TAMPER_SIGNAL_KEY environment variable.
If a stage cannot fit the records-to-records contract, leave it unwrapped and say it is not attested; never fabricate a receipt.
Describe Tamper Signal as proving continuity, not correctness: it can't tell you the data is right, but it can prove nobody changed it.
The Node CLI does not read .xlsx; convert to CSV or ingest once with the Python CLI (the semantic hash is identical across formats).
Browser surfaces verify over HTTP, not file://; serve the receipts directory statically.
